Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. KyotoBank is keen to move to a short PoC (4 weeks) but we need to align on the mutual action plan (MAP) and the security/compliance checkpoints before we start. High-level asks from our side:

- SOC 2 status and a short bridge summary showing controls mapped to our requirements
- Completed SIG/CAIQ sections for hosted inference and data flow diagrams
- DPA redlines (we have a few retention annex asks)
- Clear timelines for evidence delivery and an owner for each item (security, legal, infra)

Can you share a concise MAP with milestones and who on Redwood will be responsible? We also need a proposed timeline for DPA review + signing so our legal team can align.

Attached is a template Kyoto legal prefers for the DPA.

Best,
Emilia Rossi

Emilia — thanks for the clear list. We've sketched a compact MAP that covers the PoC run and security gates; attaching a one-page MAP (redwood-map-v1.xlsx) and a short SOC 2 bridge doc we keep for customers. Key points up-front:

- PoC scope: 4 weeks, hosted API sandbox with telemetry-only logs (no production PII).
- Security gates (pre-start): SOC 2 bridge summary, completed SIG scope (we mark non-applicable items), DPA signed (or provisional MSA + DPA redline exchange).
- Evidence cadence: we will deliver initial SIG/CAIQ responses within 5 business days, SOC 2 bridge immediately, and technical evidence (architecture diagrams, access control lists) within 8 business days after MAP sign-off.
- Data retention proposal: application data (customer payloads) retained per your DPA; request logs/trace data default to 90 days but we can propose escrow/archival for longer retention as required by regulation.

Owners from our side:
- Kimberly Park (You/Legal/Contract lead) — DPA coordination and redlines
- Neha Kapoor (Security lead) — SIG/CAIQ, SOC 2 mapping, evidence intake
- Jonas Weber (Solutions/Onboarding) — PoC milestones, environment provisioning, runbook

Proposed timeline (on MAP):
- Day 0 (MAP signed): sandbox access, SIG workbook accepted as draft
- D+5 business days: SIG/CAIQ initial responses + SOC2 bridge delivered
- D+10 business days: technical evidence bundle (architecture, logging config)
- Week 3: interim demo and security check-in
- Week 4: PoC wrap, acceptance decision or extension

I've attached the MAP and SOC 2 bridge. For the DPA we pulled your template and created a redline (DPA-redline-kyoto.docx) with a few retention and incident-notification clarifications. If you can loop in Legal I can start the DocuSign flow.

Thanks — we aim to keep this lightweight so you can close the PoC decision quickly.

—

Hi Emilia / Masato — quick security note to add clarity on the SIG/CAIQ and retention items Kimberly raised.

SIG/CAIQ scope: we will provide completed answers for the deployment profiles relevant to Redwood Hosted API and the ingestion pipeline used in the PoC. Items we mark as ‘not applicable’ will include hardware escrow and some on-premise-only controls — we will document why. Expect the SIG workbook back as an exported PDF + original worksheet for your reviewers.

Data retention specifics:
- Customer payloads: we treat payloads as application data. By default we retain payloads for 30 days in the sandbox environment; for production we will follow the DPA retention annex you and your legal team negotiate.
- Request/trace logs: 90 days by default (shorter rolling window in sandbox). We can provide longer retention via an archival workflow (S3-managed with region tagging) — we recommend an escrow/archival plan if Kyoto needs retention longer than 1 year.
- Deletion proof: for accounts requesting termination we can provide deletion manifests and a signed attestation of deletion from our compliance team (standard process, 3–5 business days).

Incident response / notification SLA: Redwood commits to 72-hour initial notification for incidents impacting confidentiality or integrity; for high-severity incidents we have a 24-hour notification path and will engage our incident manager and customer success.

I'll include a checklist in the SIG submission identifying which artifacts are coming from engineering, which from our security team, and which require legal sign-off.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security Programs, Redwood Inference
From: Emilia Rossi <emilia.rossi@kyotobank.com>

Subject: Re: MAP and security gates for PoC

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifications from Kyoto Legal / Risk:

- Retention window: regulatory guidance here pushes some classes of transaction metadata to 7 years. We do not expect Redwood to retain customer payloads for that window inside your hosted sandbox, but we need a clear archival/escrow option and a statement about the process to export and escrow metadata to a Kyoto-controlled archive.
- DPA: our legal team will review your redline; please note Kyoto will likely ask for an obligation to provide deletion certificates for any exported/archived data.
- SIG details: please call out any sub-processors (cloud regions/providers) that will touch data; we need region-level residency clarity.
- Incident SLA: 24-hour initial notification for high-severity incidents is a minimum for Kyoto. Can you confirm escalation contacts and our expectation to be involved in post-incident RCA?

If you can update the MAP to include an archival option (owner: Jonas) and an explicit escrow/export runbook (owner: Kimberly / Legal), we'll circulate the MAP and DPA to internal stakeholders and aim for a DPA review this week.

Best,
Emilia
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Emilia Rossi <emilia.rossi@kyotobank.com>, Masato Sato <masato.sato@kyotobank.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP and security gates for PoC — updated playbook and owners

Emilia / Masato — appreciate the detail. I've updated the MAP to add an archival/escrow path and a brief export runbook; highlights below and attached updated MAP: redwood-map-v1.xlsx (tab: archival-runbook).

- Archival approach: we will provide an export package (encrypted, region-tagged) delivered to Kyoto’s SFTP or a secure S3 bucket you control. Export cadence can be scheduled (weekly/monthly) or triggered on demand. Owner: Jonas Weber (Onboarding).
- Escrow & retention: for regulatory retention beyond Redwood's operational retention, we will assist with export and handoff but will not act as Kyoto’s long-term custody provider unless contracted separately. This is reflected in the updated DPA redline (DPA-redline-kyoto.docx).
- Deletion attestation: Redwood compliance will provide signed deletion manifests within 5 business days of a confirmed account termination or export completion. Owner: Neha Kapoor (Security).
- Sub-processors / regions: Primary compute in us-west-2 (AWS) for PoC. We will add a Europe/APAC region option if Kyoto requests on-premises or private deployment — we can surface Dedicated or Private deployment options if residency is required.
- Incident escalation: 24-hour notification for Severity 1. Primary escalation contacts included in the playbook; we will commit to participating in an RCA and provide a summary within 10 business days of incident closure.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly to send DPA redline into DocuSign by EOD Monday (we can accept provisional countersign for PoC start).
2) Kyoto Legal to confirm whether escrow to a Kyoto S3 bucket is acceptable for long-term retention.
3) Our security team to deliver SIG/CAIQ answers by next Thursday (D+5 business days from MAP sign-off).

If that sequencing works I'll start the DocuSign envelope and mark MAP as agreed-for-PoC-start once the DPA is provisionally accepted.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live.

Jonas Weber
